title: A normal alternating class from polynomial data
statement: Let $b\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, let $i\in\mathbb N$, and let $V$ be a language in polynomial time. Suppose $f$ is a polynomial-time computable function on bit strings, and $\ell_1,\ell_2$ are functions from bit strings to natural numbers for which the unary words $1^{\ell_1(y)}$ and $1^{\ell_2(y)}$ are polynomial-time computable from $y$. Then the language of strings $y$ for which a quantifier of type $b$ over strings $U$ of length $\ell_1(y)$ makes the depth-$i$ alternating-quantifier statement over $V$, with initial type opposite to $b$, block length $\ell_2(y)$, and input $f(\langle y,U\rangle)$ hold belongs to the alternating class at level $i+1$ with initial type $b$.
hypotheses_covered: The unary word function determined by $\ell_1$ is polynomial-time computable
The unary word function determined by $\ell_2$ is polynomial-time computable
